/-!
# Conjecture 7.21

by F. B. Cannonito

Is there an algorithm which decides if an arbitrary finitely presented solvable group is
metabelian?

A finite presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid r_1, \dots, r_k \rangle$ is encoded as
the number $n$ of generators together with a finite list of relator words in the letters
$x_i^{\pm 1}$. The question is a promise problem: an algorithm is given such a presentation,
is promised that the presented group is solvable, and must halt with the correct answer to
"is the presented group metabelian?". Nothing is required of the algorithm on presentations
of non-solvable groups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def equivSubtype :
    FinitePresentation ≃
      {q : ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool)) // ∀ w ∈ q.2, ∀ l ∈ w, l.1 < q.1} where
  toFun P := ⟨(P.numGenerators, P.relators.map (List.map fun l => (l.1.1, l.2))), by
    intro w hw l hl
    obtain ⟨w, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hw
    obtain ⟨l, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hl
    exact l.1.isLt⟩
  invFun q := ⟨q.1.1, q.1.2.pmap
    (fun w hw => w.pmap (fun l hl => (⟨l.1, q.2 w hw l hl⟩, l.2)) fun _ h => h) fun _ h => h⟩
  left_inv P := by
    cases P
    simp [List.pmap_map, List.pmap_eq_map]
  right_inv q := by
    obtain ⟨⟨n, R⟩, h⟩ := q
    simp [List.map_pmap]

theorem primrecPred_forall_lt :
    PrimrecPred fun q : ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool)) => ∀ w ∈ q.2, ∀ l ∈ w, l.1 < q.1 :=

def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=

blocks.docstring:
A group is metabelian if its commutator subgroup is abelian, i.e. if it is solvable of derived
length at most `2`.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_iff_derivedSeries_two_eq_bot (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    IsMetabelian G ↔ derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥ := by
  rw [IsMetabelian, derivedSeries_succ, derivedSeries_one,
    Subgroup.commutator_eq_bot_iff_le_centralizer, Subgroup.le_centralizer_iff_isMulCommutative]
blocks.docstring: A group is metabelian iff its second derived subgroup is trivial.

blocks.docstring:
Is there an algorithm which decides if an arbitrary finitely presented solvable group is
metabelian?

That is, is there a partial computable function `f` on finite presentations such that, for
every finite presentation `P` of a solvable group, `f` halts on `P` and outputs `true` if the
group presented by `P` is metabelian and `false` otherwise? This is a promise problem: nothing is
required of `f` on presentations of non-solvable groups.

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered, unstarred yes/no question (answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ algorithm): it is a promise problem — the algorithm takes an encoded finite presentation ⟨X | R⟩ (finitely many generators and relators, e.g. as a Primcodable/ComputablePred input) that is assumed to present a solvable group, and must correctly output whether the presented group is metabelian (derived length ≤ 2, i.e. commutator subgroup abelian); no correctness requirement is imposed on presentations of non-solvable groups, and 'algorithm' is a computable function on presentations, not a per-group Decidable instance.
claims.reviewer_why: c04 states the promise problem faithfully: a single uniform algorithm on encoded finite presentations (junk-free `FinitePresentation` structure with a standard Gödel numbering via `Primcodable.subtype`, verified by encode/decode round-trip tests), Mathlib `PresentedGroup`/`IsSolvable`, bespoke `IsMetabelian` with an API lemma tying it to `derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥`, and correctness/halting demanded only on presentations of solvable groups. Chosen over the total-`Computable` candidates (c01, c02, c03, c06, c08) because the partial-recursive reading (`Partrec f`, halting with the right answer on all solvable inputs) is the standard meaning of 'algorithm deciding a property in a class of groups' in this literature (Baumslag–Cannonito–Miller, Miller's survey); the known algorithms for f.p. solvable groups are parallel searches that need not halt on non-solvable inputs, so a total-function formalization could be false while the problem is regarded as answered 'yes'. c05 and c07 are equally faithful partial formulations; c04 was preferred for having no junk codes, the cleanest `∃ b ∈ f P` Part-membership statement, and API/test lemmas for the bespoke definitions. Only edit: a line-length wrap in `equivSubtype`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.21

by F. B. Cannonito

Is there an algorithm which decides if an arbitrary finitely presented solvable group is
metabelian?

A finite presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid r_1, \dots, r_k \rangle$ is encoded as
the number $n$ of generators together with a finite list of relator words in the letters
$x_i^{\pm 1}$. The question is a promise problem: an algorithm is given such a presentation,
is promised that the presented group is solvable, and must halt with the correct answer to
"is the presented group metabelian?". Nothing is required of the algorithm on presentations
of non-solvable groups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.21»

/--
A finite group presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid r_1, \dots, r_k \rangle$: a number
`n` of generators together with a finite list of relators, each a word in the letters
$x_i^{\pm 1}$. As in `FreeGroup.mk`, the letter `(i, true)` stands for $x_i$ and the letter
`(i, false)` stands for $x_i^{-1}$.
-/
structure FinitePresentation where
  /-- The number of generators. -/
  numGenerators : ℕ
  /-- The relators, as words in the generators and their inverses. -/
  relators : List (List (Fin numGenerators × Bool))

namespace FinitePresentation

/-- The group $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid r_1, \dots, r_k \rangle$ presented by `P`. -/
abbrev PresentedGroup (P : FinitePresentation) : Type :=
  _root_.PresentedGroup {FreeGroup.mk w | w ∈ P.relators}

/--
A finite presentation is the same thing as a pair `(n, R)` of a natural number `n` and a list
`R` of words over `ℕ × Bool` all of whose letters are `< n`.
-/
def equivSubtype :
    FinitePresentation ≃
      {q : ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool)) // ∀ w ∈ q.2, ∀ l ∈ w, l.1 < q.1} where
  toFun P := ⟨(P.numGenerators, P.relators.map (List.map fun l => (l.1.1, l.2))), by
    intro w hw l hl
    obtain ⟨w, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hw
    obtain ⟨l, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hl
    exact l.1.isLt⟩
  invFun q := ⟨q.1.1, q.1.2.pmap
    (fun w hw => w.pmap (fun l hl => (⟨l.1, q.2 w hw l hl⟩, l.2)) fun _ h => h) fun _ h => h⟩
  left_inv P := by
    cases P
    simp [List.pmap_map, List.pmap_eq_map]
  right_inv q := by
    obtain ⟨⟨n, R⟩, h⟩ := q
    simp [List.map_pmap]

/-- Checking that all letters of all relators are in range is primitive recursive. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem primrecPred_forall_lt :
    PrimrecPred fun q : ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool)) => ∀ w ∈ q.2, ∀ l ∈ w, l.1 < q.1 :=
  have h₁ : PrimrecRel fun (l : ℕ × Bool) (n : ℕ) => l.1 < n :=
    Primrec.nat_lt.comp (Primrec.fst.comp Primrec.fst) Primrec.snd
  h₁.forall_mem_list.forall_mem_list.comp Primrec.snd Primrec.fst

instance : Primcodable FinitePresentation :=
  @Primcodable.ofEquiv _ _ (Primcodable.subtype primrecPred_forall_lt) equivSubtype

end FinitePresentation

/--
A group is metabelian if its commutator subgroup is abelian, i.e. if it is solvable of derived
length at most `2`.
-/
def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsMulCommutative (commutator G)

/-- A group is metabelian iff its second derived subgroup is trivial. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_iff_derivedSeries_two_eq_bot (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    IsMetabelian G ↔ derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥ := by
  rw [IsMetabelian, derivedSeries_succ, derivedSeries_one,
    Subgroup.commutator_eq_bot_iff_le_centralizer, Subgroup.le_centralizer_iff_isMulCommutative]

/-- Metabelian groups are solvable. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsMetabelian.isSolvable {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsMetabelian G) : IsSolvable G :=
  ⟨2, (isMetabelian_iff_derivedSeries_two_eq_bot G).mp h⟩

/-- Abelian groups are metabelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsMetabelian G :=
  inferInstanceAs (IsMulCommutative (commutator G))

/--
The presentation with no generators and no relators presents the trivial group, which is
metabelian.
-/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_presentedGroup_zero_nil :
    IsMetabelian (⟨0, []⟩ : FinitePresentation).PresentedGroup :=
  haveI : Subsingleton (⟨0, []⟩ : FinitePresentation).PresentedGroup :=
    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (Quotient _))
  ⟨⟨fun _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩⟩

/--
Is there an algorithm which decides if an arbitrary finitely presented solvable group is
metabelian?

That is, is there a partial computable function `f` on finite presentations such that, for
every finite presentation `P` of a solvable group, `f` halts on `P` and outputs `true` if the
group presented by `P` is metabelian and `false` otherwise? This is a promise problem: nothing is
required of `f` on presentations of non-solvable groups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.21» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ f : FinitePresentation →. Bool, Partrec f ∧
      ∀ P : FinitePresentation, IsSolvable P.PresentedGroup →
        ∃ b ∈ f P, (b = true ↔ IsMetabelian P.PresentedGroup) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.21»

items: 'Algorithm' is formalized as a PARTIAL computable function `f : FinitePresentation →. Bool` (`Partrec f`) that must halt with the correct answer on every presentation of a solvable group (`∃ b ∈ f P, (b = true ↔ IsMetabelian …)`); on presentations of non-solvable groups it may diverge or output anything. This is the literal promise-problem semantics (Even–Selman–Yacobi) and the convention in combinatorial group theory (e.g. McKinsey-type uniform algorithms for a class of groups). The alternative reading with a TOTAL computable `f : FinitePresentation → Bool` (`Computable f ∧ ∀ P, IsSolvable → (f P = true ↔ IsMetabelian …)`) is a special case; the two readings can in principle differ (recursive separability vs. a partial decision procedure), and a reviewer should confirm the chosen one. Switching is a one-line change.

A finite presentation is encoded as `numGenerators : ℕ` together with `relators : List (List (Fin numGenerators × Bool))` (relator words in the letters x_i^{±1}, as in `FreeGroup.mk`; words need not be reduced). The presented group is Mathlib's `PresentedGroup {FreeGroup.mk w | w ∈ P.relators}` on `FreeGroup (Fin n)`. Every finite presentation is representable and every code is a genuine finite presentation (no junk codes).

The `Primcodable FinitePresentation` instance is obtained via an equivalence with the subtype of `ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool))` whose letters are all `< n`, using `Primcodable.subtype` with a proof that the range check is primitive recursive; hence the notion of algorithm is the standard one on a natural Gödel numbering of presentations.

Metabelian is defined as `IsMulCommutative (commutator G)` (commutator subgroup abelian), i.e. derived length ≤ 2; the API lemma `isMetabelian_iff_derivedSeries_two_eq_bot` confirms the equivalence with `derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥`. Solvable is Mathlib's `IsSolvable`.

The promise hypothesis `IsSolvable P.PresentedGroup` is placed after the universal quantifier over presentations; it is not vacuous (e.g. the empty presentation presents the trivial group), so the statement is not trivially satisfiable.
AMS tags 3 (mathematical logic / computability) and 20 (group theory).

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity: 'algorithm' for a promise problem can be read as a total computable function correct on the promise (c01, c02, c03, c06, c08) or a partial recursive function that must halt correctly on the promise (c04, c05, c07). The two are not obviously equivalent since the set of presentations of solvable groups is not c.e.; total ⇒ partial, so the partial reading is the more inclusive one and matches the literature's notion of 'recognizable in the class of f.p. solvable groups'. Shipped the partial reading; the decomposition table's phrase 'computable function on presentations' was read as emphasising uniformity (not a per-group Decidable instance) rather than totality. c06's and c05's reports explicitly flag this same issue. All candidates' encodings of presentations are computably inter-translatable, so the choice of encoding does not affect the truth value. Metabelian is derived length ≤ 2 (commutator subgroup abelian); trivial and abelian groups count, as is standard. No candidate omitted the slot; no omission reasons to adjudicate.
